text: B1e move, relating or contrasting: the floor read for all 197 themes (out/_analysis/b1e_floor.py, b1e_floor.tsv). 183 main: 181 on a pair of rooms at least twice apart in items in the window and not joined by an episode, T3-173 (GreenCorner, AprilKnights) and T3-189 (scp, parahumans) on form. 14 rare, each with a moved_to_rare line in tier_history.jsonl: T3-007, T3-025, T3-067, T3-077, T3-093, T3-106, T3-133, T3-144, T3-161, T3-166, T3-186, T3-191, T3-197 seen in one room, T3-128 in three rooms that tell one episode (E1132). tier_history.jsonl now 252 lines.

B1e scheme assembled: out/scheme.jsonl (197 themes: 183 main, 14 rare), out/families.jsonl (21 families), out/scheme.md (index page, then every family's themes with gate, discriminators, varies, is_not, floor and exemplars), by out/_analysis/b1e_assemble.py from the 21 drafts. Before assembly, 42 gate fields that named legs, theme ids, concept ids or notes were rewritten in words (out/_analysis/b1e_fix_fields.py), and the script cut rule 0 and bag line counts from 32 fields: the stranger is given none of these. validate.py B1 passes the scheme: every exemplar resolves, every floor holds; warnings for 10 themes with fewer than three exemplars and for T3-128 rare on three rooms (one episode, E1132). confusions.md written: 17 ranked pairs from the rule 0 and bag record (out/_analysis/b1e_confusions.py), each with an exposing second-order theme; the hardest pair is T3-005/T3-021, 131 of 655 second-order themes on both, directions 60 and 66, estimated disagreement 15 to 20%; a family boundary to test at B2: T3-010 in G14 against truces, alliances and bartering in G15.

B1e findings.jsonl opened with F-001, the scheme's claim in rule 14's form (warrant read, status standing): 197 kinds, none over 7% of the 7,786 placed second-order themes; 51.1% of themes on one kind; themes about dealing with other rooms 36.0% single against 54.1%. Bound: the multi-kind share rises with the grain of the second-order theme (70.4% single at five concepts or fewer, 35 to 38% at six to twenty), so it measures the coders' cut too. Room fit (out/_analysis/b1e_rooms_fit.py): canucks fits best (40 themes, each on one kind, 33 kinds in 18 families, about 5 concepts a theme); turkey fits worst among rooms of 8 themes or more (14 themes, 36 placements, 13 on two or three kinds, about 19 concepts a theme). Next: the stranger test.

B1e stranger test (section 7): gates and discriminators of T3-005, T3-021 and T3-087 only; five second-order themes drawn by out/_analysis/b1e_stranger_draw.py (seeded, from 689 members of the three, rooms outside the second pass and outside the three themes' exemplar rooms): thesimpsons t11, littlewitchacademia t08, vegan t08, palestine t04, WPI t05. Placed from the gates: thesimpsons t11 T3-005; littlewitchacademia t08 T3-021; vegan t08 T3-005, hesitating whether its repair concepts (c0177, c0181) earn T3-021; palestine t04 T3-005 with T3-021 (c0073), hesitating over c0074, a member messaging the placers laying blue dots, which none of the three gates holds; WPI t05 T3-005 with T3-087, hesitating whether a warning that a named room wants the logo is tracing when the source is already known. All five primaries match the working placements; the working grouping did not add T3-021 to vegan t08. Not blind: mem.py theme prints the working placements above the concepts, and they were in view.

B1e running-file entries (section 7): out/_analysis/b1e_running_dropped.py read all 769 entries of out/running-A1.md, after the whole file was read in four parts. 601 name a doing and are carried by the kinds whose gates take them; 168 are dropped, listed with their reasons in out/_analysis/b1e_running_dropped.tsv: canvas 51 (facts from the canvas record: linked artworks, writers' shares, placements before hour 0, the atlas), record 61 (remarks about the A1 reading: block markers, sides of a block, corrections, notes an account weakened), share 15 (a share of a room's record: April Fools filling most turns, one member writing most), brief 33 (the room's week before the canvas as the source of a word or mark), sequence 8 (an order of events over the week, for stage C). The doings inside dropped entries, such as attack talk in a room read as restrained, are carried by their kinds.

B1e saturation-B1.md: a closing section says how the second pass stopped, on its run of rooms that added no new third-order theme (108 rooms, 148.1 average rooms, against 78 and 72.1, floor 30; all 108 chosen rooms read). Under the rule before 2026-10-07 the two stretches of at least twenty rooms are stretches 1 and 2 (21 and 24 rooms), both with no new kind. A first draft of the paragraph named stretches 6 and 7 and a room count typed from memory; it was checked against the stretch table and corrected before this line.

B1e discriminators: out/_analysis/b1e_disc_pairs.py checked the owed pairs in both gates and found six missing in one or both directions (T3-149/T3-151, T3-038 against T3-073, T3-188/T3-195, T3-076/T3-195, T3-050/T3-017, T3-024 against T3-168). out/_analysis/b1e_add_disc.py added 10 questions to the drafts; the scheme was reassembled (scheme.jsonl, families.jsonl, scheme.md), and every owed pair now has its question in both gates.

B1e notes-B1.md: section 'Leg B1e, the scheme standing, 2026-10-11' appended (lines 2758 on; 2,755 lines before, 3,072 after): what was written, how the gates were written, the gate questions settled, the floor and tiers, moves, what the second-order themes showed that the notes did not predict, 17 ideas never minted and where their doings sit, the stranger test, the ten biggest bags, running-file entries dropped, token sizes and cuts, size distribution, families, the one second-order theme handled badly (argentina t06), faults, and the strongest two-or-half argument for every theme. The close-check report follows at the close. Next: handback-B1.md.

B1e handback-B1.md written (896 words): what the stage delivers, what was not done as the stage file says (rivals not searched in full, ten themes short of three exemplars, the stranger test not blind, B1d leftovers not re-placed, two floors on form), what is wrong with the instrument, what I ask for, and what stage B2 should know. out/interview/B1e.md written (698 words). Next: the head, then the close-check.

B1e head rewritten at 2,281 words, with no 'r/': where the run stands (B1 done, B2 next), the claim F-001, the batching paragraph and the B1b-29 rules carried, what B1 hands to B2, the floor and tiers, open and settled distinctions, ledgers, rules kept, and the next comparison. Next: the stopping report, the close-check, the report into the notes, the closing line, done.sh B1 --cut interview.

B1e close: the scheme standing. scheme.jsonl 197 themes (183 main, 14 rare) in 21 families; scheme.md, confusions.md (17 pairs; hardest T3-005/T3-021, estimated 15 to 20%), findings.jsonl F-001 (standing), handback-B1.md, out/interview/B1e.md; tier_history.jsonl 252 lines (115 relabelled, 14 moved_to_rare); validate.py B1: 0 errors, 211 warnings, report pasted into notes-B1.md (now 3,104 lines). Stage B1 is done; closing with done.sh B1 --cut interview. Next leg: stage B2, by its stage file.

B1e close refused once: done.sh read 'D1' in the head (the stage that writes prior.md sections 7 and 8) as an unresolved dimension id. The head now says 'the return stage'; no other D-id is in it. Rerunning done.sh B1 --cut interview.
